knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: CD-R2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. What does the sequence Family to eta to link represent in a generalised linear model?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: A GLM combines a response distribution, linear predictor, and link connecting the response mean to that predictor.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Choose a family, form eta = X beta, and connect mu through g(mu) = eta.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Confusing the link with a transformation of observations or predictors.

choices.label: The response family specifies mean-variance behaviour, eta = X beta is the linear predictor, and the link satisfies g(mu) = eta.
The family determines X, while the link transforms each predictor into response variance.
Eta is the observed response and the link is its density.
The link requires the response itself to be Normal.

knowledge_checks.title: Revision Checkpoint: Poisson canonical link and deviance
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. For a Poisson GLM, which statement about the canonical link and deviance is correct?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The Poisson canonical link is logarithmic, and GLM deviance is likelihood-based.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Use log(mu) = eta and interpret deviance as a likelihood comparison with the saturated fit.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating deviance as ordinary residual sum of squares or complete model validation.

choices.label: The canonical link is log(mu) = eta, and deviance compares fitted and saturated models through likelihoods.
The canonical link is mu squared = eta, and deviance is residual sum of squares in every GLM.
The identity link is the only valid Poisson link because counts are untransformed.
Small deviance proves every distributional and independence assumption.

worked_example.title: Retrieve GLM Family-eta-link and Poisson log link
worked_example.problem_statement: Closed-book retrieval. State what the sequence Family → η → link means in a generalised linear model. For a Poisson GLM, name the canonical link and state what deviance compares.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Retrieve the GLM skeleton, then the Poisson canonical link and deviance comparison.

steps.label: Retrieve Family → η → link
steps.explanation: The response family specifies mean-variance behaviour, η = Xβ is the linear predictor, and the link satisfies g(μ) = η.
steps.calculation: Family = mean-variance; η = Xβ; g(μ) = η

steps.label: Name the Poisson canonical link
steps.explanation: The Poisson canonical link is logarithmic: log(μ) = η.

steps.label: State what deviance compares
steps.attempt_cue: Deviance compares fitted work with what?
steps.explanation: GLM deviance is a likelihood comparison between the fitted model and the saturated fit. It is not ordinary residual sum of squares in every GLM.
steps.calculation: Deviance = likelihood comparison with saturated fit (not RSS-by-default)
steps.result: Deviance role retrieved; RSS collapse refused

worked_example.final_answer: Family specifies mean-variance behaviour, η = Xβ is the linear predictor, and g(μ) = η is the link. For Poisson, the canonical link is log(μ) = η, and deviance compares fitted and saturated models through likelihoods.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Treating the link as a transformation of the raw observations, or treating GLM deviance as ordinary residual sum of squares in every model.
